_doc: The fixed question bank for `smpl ask`. One narrow question per id; no measurement ever goes into a prompt. `kind`: clip (one audio frame) or ab (two, always asked in both orders). `answer`: number {min,max} | bool | enum {values}. `timestamps`: none | optional | required (required = must be non-empty when the answer is true). `route`: null (the model may be asked) | smpl (stereo / fidelity: the model hears a mono 16 kHz downmix, so smpl answers it; `ask` refuses without --allow-routed) | ear (asked, but no objective smpl measure exists, so crosscheck leaves it for the listening page). `claim`: the human-readable rendering used in claim frames and ear-ledger questions. The ids MUST equal smpl_analysis.crosscheck.QUESTIONS (a test pins it).

questions.prompt: What is the tempo of this loop in beats per minute? Give your single best estimate as one number.
Listen to the fast hits (sixteenth notes). Are they evenly spaced (straight), or do the off-beat hits lag behind to give a shuffled, swung feel?
Does any single hit land audibly early or late against the steady pulse of the loop (a flam, a drag, a loose hit)? If yes, list the time in seconds of each such hit.

claim.true: A hit lands early or late against the pulse.
claim.false: Every hit sits on the pulse.

questions.prompt: Is the pitched material in tune with standard concert pitch (A = 440 Hz)? Answer with how far off it is in cents (100 cents = one semitone): 0 if in tune, positive if sharp, negative if flat.
questions.claim: The pitched material is {answer} cents off concert pitch (negative = flat).

questions.prompt: Is there audible digital clipping (flat-topped peaks, a harsh crackle or fizz on the loud hits)? If yes and you can tell where, list the times in seconds.
Is there a click, pop, dropout or glitch that is not part of the music? If yes, list the time in seconds of each one.

claim.true: There is a click or glitch that is not part of the music.
claim.false: There is no click or glitch.

questions.prompt: Which clip is louder overall, A or B? Answer "same" if you cannot hear a difference.

claim.same: A and B are equally loud.

questions.prompt: Which clip has more swing (off-beat hits lagging behind the grid), A or B? Answer "same" if both feel alike.
Which clip has the tighter low end (a shorter, cleaner bass or kick tail with less boom), A or B? Answer "same" if both feel alike.

claim.A: A has the tighter low end.
claim.B: B has the tighter low end.
claim.same: A and B have equally tight low ends.

questions.prompt: How wide is the stereo image: mono, narrow or wide?
Is there a phase problem (a hollow, thin or cancelling sound that would collapse in mono)?
Estimate the true-peak level in dBTP.
questions.claim: The true peak is about {answer} dBTP.

questions.prompt: Above what frequency in Hz is there no content (a low-pass or lossy-codec cutoff)?
